content.title: About
content.content: Beef with mushroom sauce is a dish made from premium cuts of beef, seared to a golden crust and simmered in a fragrant sauce of mushrooms, cream, and spices. The sauce gives the dish a smooth, creamy flavor with a subtle mushroom note.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is a rich source of iron that is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.
Button mushrooms are one of the most widely cultivated edible mushrooms worldwide.
Traditionally, beef with mushroom sauce is served in French and Italian restaurants.
Cream in the sauce adds richness and helps retain the aromatic compounds of the mushrooms.
The dish is quick to prepare: searing the beef takes 5‑7 minutes, and simmering in the sauce adds another 15‑20 minutes.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals support the immune system and normal nerve function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef is rich in B12, B6, and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Mushrooms – source of vitamin D
items.content: Button mushrooms, especially when exposed to UV light, contain vitamin D, beneficial for bone health.

items.title: Cream – source of vitamin A and fat‑soluble vitamins
items.content: Cream adds vitamin A and aids the absorption of other fat‑soluble vitamins in the dish.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Cream and certain cuts of beef can raise saturated fat intake, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cream may trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Using prepared broths or soy sauces can increase the dish’s salt content.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Beef should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C to prevent salmonella and other bacterial infections.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Serve the dish hot, garnished with fresh herbs such as parsley or dill. It pairs well with mashed potatoes, rice, pasta, or a fresh vegetable side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftover beef with mushroom sauce in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer keeping, freeze for 2‑3 months. Reheat thoroughly to a rolling boil before serving to ensure safety.
